title: I Took the $11 Gamble...I Lost. Add Mine To the List of Ones That Went Into the Trash
text:
I Took the $11 Gamble...I Lost. Add Mine To the List of Ones That Went Into the Trash. I strongly recommend you not buy this Pasta Cooker.

First of all, it is really for long pastas like spaghetti, so perhaps it should be called a "Spaghetti Cooker" and not a "Pasta Cooker," since calling it a Pasta Cooker is a bit misleading. Yes, you can put in pastas like penne and shells, but since they will clump at the bottom of the container, do not expect good results. Pasta is defined as "dough made from durum wheat and water, extruded or stamped into various shapes" (key part of that is "various shapes" ... you see my point).

This product frustrated me immediately out of the box. The manufacturer decided to put a long adhesive label across the top, and then down both sides 2.5 inches. You guessed it: no way to peel it off the sides. It has to either be scraped off or Gooped/Goo-Goned. Sucks! Why do companies still use this cheap crap adhesive in 2016? Again, 2.5 inches of crap need to be scraped off on both sides!

One serving of spaghetti in this cooker will take twice as long to make versus using a pot on the stove. Perhaps that would be OK for some if the spaghetti actually came out cooked correctly and tasted the same. It doesn't.

I also tried other Pastas...and it was one failure after the next. Eventually I guess if you keep experimenting with cooking time you will eventually get the stuff cooked OK, but we shouldn't have to do that. And the taste would still be off.

For $11 it was not worth it to return a used spaghetti cooker to Amazon. So, into the trash it went.
